measurement_method.delivery: (last submitted - first submitted) / (last completed-read time - first completed-read time); excludes the first chunk from the byte numerator to match endpoints.
measurement_method.poll_rate: (last read event - first read event) / 4 / elapsed seconds, assuming consecutive full four-read groups; an inferred poll equivalent, not independently timed main-loop calls.
measurement_method.scope: Read timestamps occur after user_io_file_tx_data completes. They include transfer/ACK waits, not just read() latency. No per-word timing or physical bridge trace was captured.
measurement_method.gaps: deadline_gap_count counts delayed presentations once at eventual swap, even if multiple windows were missed; 185 is not the total count of missed frame slots.
measurement_method.first_byte: The so-named first_byte log occurs after the first entire transfer chunk. 45,532 us includes that 16 KiB transfer and is not time of first physical byte arrival; old 4 KiB values are not directly comparable.

Main_MiSTer/fpga_io.cpp:732: fast block writes omit both ACK waits
safety_findings: A direct spi_block_write substitution removes the FIFO-full backpressure handshake and is not justified by other cores using it.
spi_block_write in wide mode also truncates an odd byte count via sz/2, unlike spi_write which explicitly transmits the odd tail. Any general replacement must preserve it.
ACK timing includes physical round-trip overhead and potentially legitimate FPGA wait; current logs do not distinguish their contributions.
No helper-pipe EAGAIN does not imply the FPGA FIFO never fills: EAGAIN is observed before user_io_file_tx_data, whereas ioctl_wait is honored within its synchronous ACK loop.

corrections_to_prior_context: Entries 577-580 established a delivery ceiling but over-attributed it to the fixed per-poll byte budget. Since poll rate was derived from reads divided by four and time, matching chunk-size times inferred poll-rate to byte throughput is substantially algebraic, not independent causal proof.

The larger-buffer experiment yields ~21.80 inferred polls/s rather than ~86 Hz and only ~0.52% throughput improvement over entry 578, supporting per-byte transfer cost as the operative limit. It does not isolate pure bridge overhead from flow-control wait.
The proposed fast block-write follow-on in entries 579/580 is unsafe as a blind replacement because ACK loops enforce this core input backpressure.
The first_byte label measures first completed chunk, not first physical byte, and deadline_gap_count counts delayed presentation intervals, not every missed slot.
